title: The decision on the beach
body: On a fog-covered beach, Dr Sadao and his wife Hana find a young white man, badly wounded, whose cap bears the faint letters 'U.S. Navy'. He is an escaped prisoner of war. Sadao says that if they sheltered him they would be arrested, and if they handed him over he would certainly die. Both agree that the kindest thing would be to put him back into the sea, yet neither moves. Sadao admits that if the man were whole he could give him to the police without difficulty, 'But since he is wounded...'. Hana then says they must carry him into the house and tell the servants that they intend to give him to the police, 'as indeed we must', for the sake of the children and Sadao's position. Sadao agrees that he would not think of doing anything else, and together they lift the light, half-starved body and carry it inside.

title: Sadao on the veranda
body: After the prisoner has rowed away, Sadao watches the little island at dusk and sees no prick of light, so he knows the young man is gone, safe. Standing on the veranda, he remembers other white faces from his years in America: the dull professor at whose house he met Hana, the professor's talkative wife, his old anatomy teacher who insisted on mercy with the knife, and his fat, slatternly landlady who had nursed him through influenza but whom he still found repulsive. He recalls how hard it was to find lodgings because he was Japanese. Then he remembers the haggard face of his prisoner, 'white and repulsive', and thinks: 'Strange. I wonder why I could not kill him?'
